text: Antoine Lavoisier dethroned the phlogiston theory in the 1770s by weighing reactions before and after combustion; the conserved mass forced chemists to treat oxygen as the agent of burning rather than invoking a released fluid.

queries.text: who overturned phlogiston by quantitative weighing experiments and which element took its explanatory role
lavoisier phlogiston oxygen combustion conservation mass weigh

text: The law of conservation of mass, formalised by Lavoisier in the Traite elementaire de chimie in 1789, became the bedrock axiom that all subsequent stoichiometry assumed without further argument.

queries.text: which 1789 textbook codified the mass conservation axiom that stoichiometry would lean on for two centuries
lavoisier conservation mass traite chimie stoichiometry axiom 1789

text: John Dalton proposed the atomic theory between 1803 and 1808, fixing indivisible atoms with element-specific weights as the ontology chemists would use to read combining ratios.

queries.text: who proposed that elements are built from indivisible atoms with characteristic weights in the early 1800s
dalton atomic theory atom weight combining ratio 1803 indivisible

text: Dalton's 1808 A New System of Chemical Philosophy is still the canonical citation for the law of multiple proportions; later historians lean on it to date the shift from equivalent weights to atomic weights.

relationships.source: A New System of Chemical Philosophy

text: Amedeo Avogadro proposed in 1811 that equal volumes of gases at equal temperature and pressure contain equal numbers of particles; the hypothesis later canonised as Avogadro's law separated molecule from atom a full half-century before the discipline accepted the distinction.

queries.text: which 1811 proposal linked equal gas volumes to equal particle counts and split molecules from atoms
avogadro law equal volume gas molecule atom particle 1811

text: Stanislao Cannizzaro revived Avogadro's hypothesis at the 1860 Karlsruhe Congress, handing out a pamphlet that finally let chemists reconcile atomic weights and molecular formulas after decades of drift.

queries.text: which 1860 congress and advocate pulled Avogadro's hypothesis back into mainstream chemistry
cannizzaro karlsruhe avogadro pamphlet atomic weight reconcile 1860

text: Dmitri Mendeleev published the periodic table in 1869, ordering elements by atomic weight and leaving deliberate gaps whose predicted properties matched gallium and germanium within a decade.

queries.text: who arranged the elements into a periodic table in 1869 and which predicted elements later confirmed it
mendeleev periodic table 1869 gap gallium germanium predict element

text: Mendeleev opted to order by atomic weight but reversed tellurium and iodine on chemical grounds; later Henry Moseley re-anchored the table on atomic number, vindicating the swap without overturning the scheme.

queries.text: which pair of elements did Mendeleev swap against their atomic weights and whose later work justified it
mendeleev tellurium iodine swap moseley atomic number weight

text: August Kekule reported in 1865 that benzene's six carbons form a closed ring with alternating double bonds, a structural insight he famously credited to a daydream of a snake biting its own tail.

queries.text: who first proposed that benzene closes into a six-carbon ring with alternating double bonds
kekule benzene ring six carbon double bond 1865 snake dream

queries.text: whose 1884 ionic-dissociation thesis was dismissed at defence yet later won a chemistry Nobel
arrhenius electrolytic dissociation uppsala nobel 1903 ion conduction

text: Arrhenius framed acids as proton donors in aqueous solution and bases as hydroxide donors; the definition ruled textbooks until Bronsted-Lowry broadened acids to any proton donor regardless of solvent.

queries.text: which definition of acids did Arrhenius propose and which later framework broadened it beyond water
arrhenius acid base proton hydroxide bronsted lowry definition aqueous

text: Fritz Haber demonstrated direct ammonia synthesis from nitrogen and hydrogen in 1909; Carl Bosch scaled the process at BASF by 1913, decoupling nitrogen fertiliser from Chilean saltpetre imports.

queries.text: which 1909-1913 pair industrialised direct ammonia synthesis and what import did it displace
haber bosch ammonia synthesis nitrogen hydrogen basf saltpetre 1913

text: BASF ran the Haber-Bosch loop over a promoted iron catalyst near 200 atmospheres and 450 degrees Celsius; the osmium catalyst Haber used in the lab demo was deemed too scarce for tonnage production.

haber bosch iron osmium catalyst basf ammonia industrial 200 atm

text: Leo Baekeland filed his Bakelite patent in 1907, describing the first wholly synthetic thermoset from a phenol and formaldehyde condensation that cures into an infusible, insulating solid.

queries.text: who patented the first fully synthetic thermoset in 1907 and which two monomers did it condense
baekeland bakelite phenol formaldehyde thermoset 1907 synthetic patent

text: Bakelite found early traction as insulation in radio housings and electrical switchboards because its cross-linked network refused to flow once cured, a property that predecessors like celluloid lacked entirely.

queries.text: which early electrical applications relied on Bakelite and which plastic did it outperform on heat
bakelite radio insulation switchboard celluloid thermoset cross link

text: Irving Langmuir and Katharine Blodgett refined monolayer transfer at General Electric in the 1930s, producing the Langmuir-Blodgett film technique that still anchors modern studies of molecular thin films.

queries.text: which two General Electric scientists developed the monolayer-transfer film technique that bears their names
langmuir blodgett film monolayer general electric thin film 1930s

text: Langmuir-Blodgett deposition works by compressing an amphiphilic monolayer on a water surface then dipping a substrate through it; each pass lays down one molecular layer in controlled orientation.

queries.text: how does Langmuir-Blodgett deposition put down a single molecular layer with controlled orientation

pauling nature chemical bond resonance hybridisation electronegativity 1939

pauling electronegativity scale fluorine caesium bond dissociation energy

text: Karl Ziegler and Giulio Natta won the 1963 Nobel in Chemistry for the titanium-aluminium Ziegler-Natta catalysts that polymerise ethylene and propylene at low pressure with stereoregular control previously unavailable.

ziegler natta catalyst titanium aluminium polyethylene polypropylene 1963 nobel

text: Robert Woodward and Roald Hoffmann published the Woodward-Hoffmann rules between 1965 and 1969, orbital-symmetry arguments that explain why pericyclic reactions proceed suprafacially or antarafacially under thermal versus photochemical conditions.

queries.text: which pair published orbital-symmetry rules that govern thermal and photochemical pericyclic selectivity
woodward hoffmann orbital symmetry pericyclic suprafacial photochemical

woodward hoffmann pericyclic 4n 2 suprafacial photochemical thermal

noyori binap ruthenium asymmetric hydrogenation 2001 nobel sharpless knowles

grubbs schrock chauvin ruthenium alkylidene metathesis 2005 nobel

chauvin mechanism metathesis metallacyclobutane grubbs ligand intermediate

sharpless meldal copper azide alkyne cycloaddition click 2001 2002

text: Richard Heck, Ei-ichi Negishi, and Akira Suzuki shared the 2010 Nobel in Chemistry for palladium-catalysed cross-coupling reactions that knit aryl halides to carbon nucleophiles with unprecedented generality.

heck negishi suzuki palladium cross coupling 2010 nobel aryl halide
